correctness.rationale: The finite-monoid top Green class is exactly the units; an arc stays in its class or increases it, so no nonunit is a possible root. Independently, the outgoing weighted Laplacian with the unit root deleted is block upper triangular in a linear extension of the classes. Each non-top diagonal block of size w is (wt+Q)I−t11^T and has determinant Q(wt+Q)^(w−1); the top principal minor gives u^(u−2)t_U^(u−1) for u≥2 and is the empty determinant 1 for u=1. These are polynomial identities, hence cover zero specializations as well. The graph-tree cofactor gives the toward-root enumerator. Evaluating at ones yields the count, and setting t=1 and dividing by that evaluation gives independent class-level exit vectors with precisely the optional and compulsory categorical factors asserted. The formula does not require independence of individual parents.
residual_risks: The uploaded weighted numeric and small-monoid tests are illustrations rather than the universal proof; none is used as a premise here.

evidence: The general SCC theorem works with separate variables for all original arcs and contracts the external predecessors to one auxiliary root per noninitial component; the forest roots are selected inside the component.
Degree-weighted Cayley counts all labelled trees with monomial product of the vertex variables to their degrees; Avron–Dershowitz give the corresponding complete-graph forest count.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Combine all aux-root arc weights at a vertex: their sum is Q, the same at every vertex of the class. Reversing back, for a complete graph directed toward root r with weight x_parent on each arc, the monomial is x_r times the product of each x_i to degree_i−1. Thus the prior Cayley identity gives x_r(sum x_i)^(N−2). Put N=w+1, x_r=Q and x_i=t inside the class to give precisely Q(wt+Q)^(w−1), with the known Cayley unit-class factor as well.
